q: Which object in TheHive is normally the durable investigation record?
options: The single source alert that first reached the queue
An analyzer result before it is attached to a case
The case with its evidence, assignments and decisions
The receiving service's message confirming the run was scheduled
explanation: A case can contain evidence and work from multiple related alerts.

q: Two alerts have the same digest but different sources and times. How should their case association be decided?
options: Drop the alert that arrived later because the digest already exists
Compare the evidence and preserve separate source references
Merge the two sources into one record without indicating any difference
Use the digest match as proof that both describe the same interaction
explanation: Shared observable value is context and does not erase distinct observations.

q: Which description best fits an observable in a case?
options: A typed value relevant to the investigation
A confirmed statement of compromise approved by the incident lead
A command that the operator must run whenever a case opens
A durable authorisation allowing any responder to act on the case
explanation: An observable can be legitimate and needs provenance and context.

q: A Cortex analyzer reports a match in historical evidence. What does it support?
options: Proof that the current employee took the action under investigation
Authority to make any related change to the affected workstation
A determination that every earlier case used the same source data
A contextual finding whose currency and relevance need review
explanation: The report applies to its observable and source, with timestamps and limits.

q: What distinguishes a responder from an analyzer conceptually?
options: An analyzer determines which roles can own a case
Responders only report historical context about a digest
A responder can perform an action with a side effect
An analyzer always has unrestricted access to every case record
explanation: Operational effects require scope, permission and a verification path.

q: An integration's responder says it sent a task to another service. What establishes the intended effect?
options: A completed status is displayed in the Cortex run history
The correct task exists in the owning service
The name of the original analyst matches the target service's name
An inventory lookup returns the same queue owner's department
explanation: Execution status alone does not prove target state.

q: What belongs with a new task's completion criterion?
options: The evidence or report pointer used to confirm it
The full email message copied to the broad notification channel
A rule that every remaining case task uses the same timestamp
A note that the task can be closed without operator review
explanation: A verifiable criterion supports accountable work and handoff.

q: An internal analyzer returns an empty result, but its connection failed. What should be reported?
options: No matching record exists in the historical index
A positive match was found but cannot be displayed
The case can close because the lookup result was empty
Unable to determine; record the dependency failure
explanation: A source failure cannot establish a completed negative search.

q: Which information should be attached to a digest observable?
options: The full directory of employees granted case access
The approval role for any potential future organisational change
Type, observed value reference and source context
A final forensic conclusion derived from its filename alone
explanation: Source and type let analysts interpret why the value matters.

q: A case analyst may view a file but the lookup service is unapproved. What should happen?
options: Submit it because permission to view implies permission to share
Keep it in scope and use approved internal analysis or review
Copy it to several adjacent cases to avoid using the integration
Publish its digest and case context while waiting for a decision
explanation: Access to evidence and approval to transfer it are distinct.

q: Why should a case record preserve the external alert identifier?
options: A later reviewer can locate the original signal
It grants the system permission to change connected services
It makes any verified effect independent of the target state
It ensures all alerts under a case are duplicate deliveries
explanation: A stable external reference supports traceability into the source.

q: A request approved action on an observable, but the responder is configured on a case. What must be checked?
options: Whether the case title includes the name of the affected application
Whether every linked observable has at least one analyzer result
Whether the approving role is named anywhere in the entire organisation
The actual responder target and approved effect
explanation: The selected case context may differ from the scope that receives the action.

q: What should a reviewer read alongside a classifier's result?
options: Only the final letter assigned to its classification
The name of a similar document from a different case
Input identity, provenance, time and coverage
The employee's normal shift schedule without the evidence
explanation: A classification is interpretable when its input and conditions are known.

q: A prior case's analysis matches an item in a new case with different access rules. What is the correct next step?
options: Copy the entire earlier case because the observable is the same
Confirm authorised reuse and share only permitted context
Grant the second case all permissions of the first case automatically
Discard the new observation because there is already an analyzer report
explanation: A common value cannot broaden case access or sharing authority.

q: Which outcome best describes a valid completed no-match?
options: The named approved source returned no matching record
The provider never received or answered the query
Every source in the industry reports a clean result
The investigation cannot document a case because no tool answered
explanation: A completed no-match is limited to the actual search and source.

q: A responder times out after potentially creating its task. What should the owner do before retrying?
options: Run the same responder for every case until a green result appears
Close the receiving assignment because no acknowledgment arrived
Change the task scope so the same run can count as a fresh action
Reconcile the downstream task by its stable reference
explanation: A retry is safe only when prior effect uncertainty is addressed.

q: Which role generally determines whether case tasks are complete?
options: The first alert that arrived when the system queued the case
A digest lookup whose report uses the strongest confidence label
An authorised case owner using the task evidence
The exported list of all observables across unrelated investigations
explanation: The case owner evaluates the completion evidence and remaining work.

q: The attached analysis is old but accurately matches an exact digest. How should the analyst use it?
options: Delete all current endpoint signals because one prior assessment was benign
Preserve the match and evaluate present context separately
Treat the report as a fresh query with the date of the current incident
Assume it identifies the recipient responsible for current events
explanation: A historical artifact match and present device behaviour answer different questions.

q: Where should authorization for a consequential responder be recorded?
options: In a scoped case decision linked to the specific request
In an informal label on another observably similar case
In the report's title after the action has already executed
Only in the analyst's memory for urgent cases
explanation: A scoped decision provides reviewable evidence of action authority.

q: A duplicate alert should not produce a second task. Which signal proves that requirement?
options: Two queue items show the same text in their title fields
Both analyzer runs received a matching digest response
The second alert was deleted before it could be audited
One task exists and both receipts link to it
explanation: Inspecting the verified effect tests duplicate handling directly.

q: Which action helps preserve reporting permissions across teams?
options: Attach every received artifact to a general notification
Copy another team's full case instead of using a scoped summary
Link sensitive evidence through a restricted case reference
Make every analyzer report available to all staff by default
explanation: Restricted references let eligible reviewers reach evidence without sending it to a wider audience.

q: A case receives two analyzer outputs, one valid and one unavailable. How should the summary present them?
options: Average both results into a single alert priority score
Record the completed finding and the separate coverage gap
Report both sources as clean because one returned nothing concerning
Discard the valid finding to keep the two statuses consistent
explanation: Each source has its own outcome, relevance and limits.

q: Why should a responder report include its action time?
options: It ties the reported effect to a traceable execution
It replaces the timestamp recorded in the original alert event
It lets the operator assume all parties approved before that time
It identifies the person who authored an attached email message
explanation: An action time helps locate and reconcile the downstream evidence.

q: The receiving task exists under a different case ID. What needs to happen?
options: Mark it verified because the task text matches the request wording
Use the incorrect case as proof that approval was valid for both
Rewrite the original request to fit the incorrect case after execution
Record the target mismatch and investigate scope and recovery
explanation: Verification must confirm the actual intended target and effect.

q: What is the safest purpose for a paper integration exercise?
options: Try real transfers to see whether a provider accepts the connection
Discover which restricted inputs escape the organisation's policy review
Practise linking evidence, decisions and expected effects
Test consequential changes on production assets without a case owner
explanation: Synthetic cases let students verify reasoning without operational side effects.
